findings.description: The saboteur red result independently proves only the headline v1 byte-hold, but the section itself shows all five cases invoke the real stamper on their own copied scope and carry case-specific assertions, so the narrower mutation result does not leave the rubric unmet.

Although Bash replaces rather than appends an EXIT trap, each replacement explicitly repeats every earlier scope variable, so cleanup remains guaranteed for all scopes allocated at each execution point.

Placement alone proves only temporal inclusion, but the after-run recursive find-and-hash comparison re-enumerates the fixture tree, so a newly left regular fixture copy or a write to an existing fixture would differ from the snapshot baseline and fail the guard.
